findings.location: s7-s15 (Worked Examples, Error Analysis, Guided and Independent Practice)
findings.quote: traveled to Liberia in 1822 with 50 LD in his pocket ... 50 LD - 10 LD = 40 LD
findings.issue: Nine of seventeen sections are money-subtraction arithmetic unrelated to the founding of Liberia. No practice addresses any objective. The Error Analysis is about subtraction mistakes. The lesson cannot teach or assess its history objectives.

findings.quote: traveled to Liberia in 1822 with 50 LD
findings.issue: Anachronism: there was no Liberian dollar in 1822 (Liberia was an ACS colony; an independent currency came after 1847). Also gives settlers Liberian names (Boimah, Pewee, Zoe) as 'young man from the United States'.

findings.quote: Paul Cuffe ... worked with the ACS to promote the idea of a colony in Africa, and he helped to recruit settlers for the new colony.
findings.issue: Paul Cuffe died in 1817, years before the 1822 settlement; his 1815-16 voyage took settlers to Sierra Leone, not Liberia. He did not recruit settlers for Liberia. Verify.

findings.quote: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, a freed slave who became one of the first governors of Liberia.
findings.issue: Roberts was born free in Norfolk, Virginia (1809); he was the first Black (non-white) governor of the Commonwealth (1841) and the first President of independent Liberia (1848). Calling him a freed slave is wrong and 'one of the first governors' omits the key fact. Verify.

findings.quote: arrived on the shores of the St. Paul River ... The river that runs through the city of Monrovia is the St. Paul River.
findings.issue: The 1820 Elizabeth group went first to Sherbro Island (Sierra Leone); the 1822 landing was at Providence Island / Cape Mesurado at the mouth of the Mesurado River. The Mesurado, not the St. Paul, is the river at Monrovia; the St. Paul lies to the north (Bushrod Island between them). St. Paul River settlements (e.g. Caldwell) came later.

findings.quote: In 1822, the ACS established the colony of Liberia, which was named after the Latin word 'liber'
findings.issue: Settlement began 1822 (land at Cape Mesurado acquired Dec 1821), but the names Liberia and Monrovia were adopted in 1824. Date compression should be precise. Verify.

findings.quote: The ACS believed that Africa was the natural home ... provide a new home for freed slaves and promote Christianization
findings.issue: Presents only benevolent motives. Omits that many ACS backers (including slaveholders) wanted to remove free Black people from the US, and that most free Black Americans opposed colonisation. Mixed motives are central to G7 historical thinking. Also 'freed slaves' omits free-born African Americans and recaptured Africans (Congoes).

findings.quote: Civilization: the idea that Western culture is superior to African culture
findings.issue: Mis-defines the ordinary word 'civilization'; conflates it with the 'civilising mission' ideology. Learners will acquire a wrong word meaning. The 'rule' framing (maths template) is also wrong: it was an ideology, not an ACS rule.

findings.quote: conflict with local tribes ... courageous men and women ... pioneers
findings.issue: Settler-centred narrative; indigenous peoples (Dei, Bassa, Vai, Kru, Gola, etc.) appear only as 'local tribes' in 'conflict'. Omits how land was obtained (Dec 1821 treaty with King Peter under duress) and indigenous resistance and perspectives. 'Tribes' is a loaded term.

findings.quote: the country's struggle for independence and its experiences during the colonial era
findings.issue: Misleading: Liberia declared independence on 26 July 1847 from the ACS without a war of independence and was not colonised by a European power. 'Colonial era' framing invites misconception.

findings.quote: Analyze the challenges ... the establishment of a new government.
findings.issue: Disease (high mortality), conflict and government (Ashmun, 1839 Commonwealth, 1847 Declaration and Constitution) are only listed, never taught. No sources, dates timeline or evidence task.

findings.quote: What was the main goal of the American Colonization Society
findings.issue: Only two unkeyed exit questions address the topic; none checks the main misconceptions (Liberia as never-colonised paradise, settlers as all ex-slaves, ACS purely benevolent).

findings.quote: align with the MOE codes LR-CIV-G7_9-01 and LR-CIV-G7_9-02
findings.issue: Learner-facing claim of alignment to unverified codes; -02 (constitution comparison) is not addressed at all.

findings.quote: What is the name of the market where you can find ... palm oil fried rice?
findings.issue: Trivia warm-up not linked to prerequisite knowledge (e.g. slavery in the US, map of West African coast). Reading level high (FK 14.2 noted).
Grammar error; 'Boima' is used as an elderly woman's name in s1 and 'Boimah' as an American settler in s8 (inconsistent).
